options: Athena determining which S3 sub-prefixes are relevant to a query's filter and skipping the rest before scanning
Deleting old partitions from S3 to save storage cost
A process that compresses every file within a partition
Automatically merging small files within a partition into larger ones
questions.explain: Partition pruning is Athena skipping irrelevant S3 sub-prefixes based on the query's WHERE clause, before any data is scanned.

questions.q: In a Hive-style partitioned table, how is partition structure represented in S3?
options: As key=value pairs in the object key prefix, e.g. year=2024/month=01/
In a separate JSON index file stored alongside the data
As a hidden metadata field inside each Parquet file
Partitions cannot be represented in S3 at all, only in a database
questions.explain: Hive-style partitioning uses key=value segments directly in the S3 key prefix, which Athena and Glue crawlers recognize automatically.

questions.q: What does MSCK REPAIR TABLE do?
options: Scans S3 to discover partitions that exist as prefixes but aren't yet registered in the Catalog, and adds them
Repairs corrupted Parquet files automatically
Deletes all existing partitions and recreates the table from scratch
Converts a table from CSV format to Parquet format
questions.explain: MSCK REPAIR TABLE performs an S3 scan to find and register partitions that aren't yet known to the Catalog.

questions.q: How does partition projection differ from MSCK REPAIR TABLE?
options: It computes valid partition values from a defined pattern instead of scanning S3 to discover them, avoiding a slowdown at high partition counts
It requires manually listing every partition value by hand in the console
It only works with CSV-formatted tables
It is functionally identical to MSCK REPAIR TABLE with a different name
questions.explain: Partition projection computes expected partition values from a rule rather than scanning S3, which scales better as partition counts grow.

questions.q: Why would filtering only on customer_id provide no benefit from a table partitioned by year/month/day?
options: Partition pruning only applies to filters on the actual partition key columns, so a filter on a non-partition column can't limit which prefixes are scanned
Athena cannot filter on customer_id under any circumstances
Partitioned tables cannot be filtered on non-partition columns at all
customer_id filters always scan less data than date filters, regardless of partitioning
questions.explain: Pruning only kicks in when a query filters on the partition key itself — filtering on an unrelated column gives Athena no way to skip S3 prefixes.
